policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere ל֣וֹ is the preposition with 3ms suffix, “to him” (R/Sp3ms); ketiv לא is the negative “not” (Tn, Strong 3808), before צָ֗ר. ASV’s text, “In all their affliction he was afflicted”, reads the qere, and its footnote on this verse, “Another reading is, In all their adversity he was no adversary”, names the ketiv as the reading not adopted. The mapped note distinguishes them explicitly.
